blocks.text: Dear Ms. Hall:

This letter confirms the terms on which we will carry out an experience study of your benefit plan, and it asks for your signature so that we can begin. It follows the conversation we had this winter about reviewing how the plan's actual experience compares with the assumptions now in use. None of what follows should surprise you; it puts in writing what we discussed, so that you and we work from the same record from the first day of the study to the last. We have set out what the study covers, how we will do it, who will do the work, and what it will cost.
What the Study Covers

An experience study looks back at what the plan's members actually did and compares it with what the current assumptions predicted. We will examine the plan's recent experience in the areas that drive its cost: retirement, termination, disability, mortality, and the pattern of salary increases. For each of these, we will measure the experience the data show, weigh it against the assumption in force, and tell you where the two diverge by enough to warrant a change. We will not recommend a change where the experience does not support one, and we will say so plainly when that is the case.
The study has four parts, and our report will document each of them:

items: The member and financial data your office provides, which we reconcile and rely upon, with that reliance stated plainly in the report.
The current assumptions and the plan provisions that bear on them, taken as they are written today.
The measured experience over the study period, tabulated so that a reader can trace each rate back to the counts beneath it.
Our recommendations, set apart from the measurements so that no one mistakes a judgment for a fact.

blocks.text: How We Will Do the Work

We keep three things separate in everything we deliver, and this study is no exception. What the data show is one thing. What we have assumed is a second. What we conclude is a third. The report will present them in that order and keep them apart, so that you can see which of the three any recommendation rests on. A recommendation to change an assumption will name the experience that supports it and the judgment we brought to it, and it will never dress one up as the other. The work will be performed under the Actuarial Standards of Practice that govern an experience study of this kind.

You will receive two things at the end. The first is a written report that sets out the experience we measured, the assumptions we reviewed, and the changes we recommend, with the reasoning for each. The second is a workbook of exhibits that supports every rate in the report, so that your own advisors can follow the arithmetic. We will also present the results to your board once and answer the questions that come out of that meeting.
The Data We Will Rely On

A study is only as sound as the records under it. We will rely on the member data and the financial records that your staff at Estes Group provide, and we will reconcile them before we use them. We do not audit your data. What we do is check it for internal consistency and against the prior study, and document what we relied on, so that the basis of the work is visible to anyone who reads it. Where a record is unclear, we will come back to you rather than guess, because a study built on a guess is worth less than one that waited a week for the answer.
Who Will Do the Work

David Sherman, a senior analyst in our firm, will build and reconcile the study workbook and document the data we rely on. Jeffrey Ochoa, an actuarial analyst, will carry the modeling and run the observed experience against the current assumptions, chasing any surprising result back to the input that produced it. Megan Dudley, an actuarial associate, will prepare the exhibits and the data checks that sit beneath their work. I will review what they produce and sign the study. The professional responsibility for what we conclude is mine, and I take it seriously enough to send drafts back until the qualifications are right.
Our Fee and When We Begin

Our fee for the study is {{fact:f:E-2019-001.fee}}, which covers the work described above through delivery of the report and one presentation of the results to your board. Subject to your signature on this letter, we will begin the work on {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}}. Our first step is to request the member and financial data and to confirm the plan provisions the assumptions rest on. If the scope grows beyond what is set out here, we will agree the change and any added fee with you in writing before we do the added work, so that no invoice ever arrives for something you did not expect.
Billing and Payment

We invoice monthly for the prior month's work, and each invoice is due within thirty days of its date. If a question about an invoice comes up, tell us and we will work it through before it becomes a dispute.
Term and Termination

This agreement takes effect on the date you sign it and runs until we have delivered the study and you have paid our final invoice for it. Either of us may end it earlier on written notice to the other. If the engagement ends before the study is finished, you will owe us for the work done up to that point, and we will hand over what we have in a form you can use.
Confidentiality

We will hold what you give us in confidence and use it only for this study. Inside the firm, access is limited to the people named above and to anyone whose work on the study requires it. We will not disclose your information outside the firm without your consent, except where the law or our professional standards require it, and if that happens we will tell you unless we are barred from doing so.
Limitation of Liability

Our liability to you arising out of this engagement, whether framed in contract or in negligence, will not exceed the total fees you pay us under it, except in the case of our fraud or willful misconduct. Neither of us will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss. Any claim must be brought within one year of the delivery of the report.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our office sits, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Before either of us starts a proceeding, we will try to settle the matter through discussion between people who have the authority to resolve it.

If these terms match your understanding, please sign both copies where shown, keep one for your records, and return the other to me. If anything here reads differently from what you expected, call me before you sign and we will settle it first. We are glad to be doing this work for you, and we will give it the care it deserves.
Sincerely,

To: Jeffrey Ochoa, Megan Dudley
From: David Sherman
Re: Estes Group experience study
What We Are Doing

This memo sets the plan for the {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} experience study and assigns the work. The goal is a report the board can act on: a review of the plan's recent retirement, termination, disability, mortality, and salary experience against the assumptions now in force, with recommendations where the two diverge. The deliverables are that report and a workbook of exhibits that supports every rate in it. The study is a look-back over the observation period the client confirms, so the first job is to fix that window and the population inside it before any rate is computed.

We do this the way we do every study. What the experience shows, what the plan assumes, and what we recommend are three separate things, and they stay separate in the workbook and in the report. If a rate surprises us, we find the reason before it reaches a page. A number we cannot explain is not a finding; it is an open question, and it stays open until it is answered.

Barbara Hall, the Chief Operating Officer at Estes Group, is our point of contact. Data requests and scheduling go through her office. Any client-facing question goes through me before it goes to her, so that we speak with one voice on scope and timing.
Assignments
Here is how the work divides:

items: Data. I will reconstruct the member census and the plan's financial records, reconcile both, and document our reliance. I tie the counts to the prior study and to the client's own summaries, and I flag any gap before anything is tabulated.

Modeling. Jeffrey Ochoa builds the study model and runs the observed experience against the current assumptions. He sets no result as final until it is reviewed, and he traces any surprising rate back to the data behind it.

Exhibits and checks. Megan Dudley prepares the experience exhibits and the data checks beneath the modeling. She raises anything that does not reconcile rather than carrying it forward, and her questions are welcome the moment she has them.

blocks.text: What Gates the Work

Two things gate the rest. The first is complete member and financial data from Estes Group. The second is a clean confirmation of the plan provisions the current assumptions rest on. Until both are in hand, we tabulate nothing and treat every assumption as provisional. Data quality is the usual risk on a first study for a client; expect the census to need a pass for status codes and for members whose records do not agree with the summary. On the financial side, the contribution and withdrawal history has to distinguish a refunded member from one who left a balance in the fund, because the termination experience turns on that split. We raise anything unclear with Barbara Hall's office early rather than carry it into the model.
Where We Start

Work begins on {{fact:f:E-2019-001.start}}. The data request goes to Barbara Hall's office that week; it will list the member fields and the financial records we need and the format we want them in. Jeffrey Ochoa drafts the assumption inventory for review before any assumption is treated as settled. Megan Dudley sets up the exhibit shells so that the numbers drop into a form we can check as they arrive. In the first two weeks I expect us to load the census, tie it to the prior study, and open a short list of data questions for the client; I will keep that list on our running thread so nothing waits on a request no one has sent. We hold the study until the data and the plan provisions are both confirmed.

To: Barbara Hall
Cc: Jeffrey Ochoa, Megan Dudley
Good morning Barbara,

We have started the Estes Group experience study, and the first data extract your office sent is loading cleanly. Jeffrey Ochoa has the model shell up, and I am reconciling the member counts against last year's records. Before we go further, there are two points on the data where I need your help.

items: The member file uses a status code we cannot read with confidence. Could you confirm how it distinguishes active members from those who have terminated with a deferred benefit?
The observation window is not stated in the extract. Please confirm the first and last plan years you want the experience drawn from, so we measure against the period you intend.

blocks.text: Once we have those two answers, the census for the {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} study is settled on our end, and Megan Dudley can begin the reconciliation in earnest. Neither point is urgent this week.
Best

To: Barbara Hall
Cc: David Sherman, Jeffrey Ochoa
Hello Barbara,
Thank you for clarifying the status codes so quickly. With that in hand, the member file reconciles to your summary line for line, and we can treat the active and deferred groups as settled.

One more thing would help us before we start tabulating. A handful of records show a termination date but no benefit commencement, and we want to be sure we count them the way your office intends rather than guessing. Could you tell us whether those members are still owed a deferred benefit or whether they took their money out? David Sherman flagged them yesterday, and Jeffrey Ochoa would rather build the assumption around the real answer than around ours.
If you can point us to whoever keeps the payment records at Estes Group, we will take the detail up with them directly and keep the {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} study moving.
Best

To: Barbara Hall
Cc: Jeffrey Ochoa, Megan Dudley
Good morning Barbara,

That answers it, thank you. The records with a termination date and no commencement are deferred benefits, so we will count them as your office does, and the member data for the Estes Group study is now closed on our end.

The next piece we need is on the financial side. To set the salary-increase experience against the assumption, Jeffrey Ochoa needs the pay records for the study period, and Megan Dudley needs the contribution and withdrawal detail to tie out the fund's cash flow. Whatever format your system exports is fine; we would rather reconcile from your native report than ask your staff to reshape it for us.

There is no rush on this before next week. Once it is in hand, we begin tabulating the {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} experience and can give you a first read on where the current assumptions are holding and where they are not.
Best

To: Barbara Hall
Cc: David Sherman, Jeffrey Ochoa
Hello Barbara,
The pay file came through, thank you, and it opens without trouble. That covers what Jeffrey Ochoa needs for the salary-increase side, so he can start there while I work the rest.

The one piece still open is the withdrawal detail. The contribution history you sent is complete, but the file does not separate a member who left and took a refund from one who left the balance in the fund, and that distinction is exactly what the termination experience turns on. If your system can export the withdrawal transactions with a reason code, that would settle it cleanly for the Estes Group study.
Send it whenever it is convenient, and I will reconcile it against the census the same day, so we can close the {{fact:f:E-2019-001.client}} data and move to the tabulation.
Best
